title: Stars & Galaxies
blurb: Stellar life cycles, nebulae and constellations

questions.question: What is the name of the galaxy we live in?
questions.fact: The Milky Way is a barred spiral galaxy about 100,000 light-years across.

questions.question: What is the nearest star to Earth?
questions.fact: After the Sun, the nearest star is Proxima Centauri, about 4.24 light-years away.

questions.question: Which star is commonly called the North Star?
questions.fact: Polaris sits almost directly above Earth's north pole, so it barely moves in the night sky.

questions.question: A light-year is a unit of…
questions.fact: A light-year is the distance light travels in one year — about 9.46 trillion km.

questions.question: What colour are the hottest stars?
questions.fact: Blue stars can exceed 30,000 °C, while red stars are the coolest at around 3,000 °C.

questions.question: What is the brightest star in the night sky?
questions.fact: Sirius, the 'Dog Star', is bright because it is both luminous and only 8.6 light-years away.

questions.question: What is the nearest large spiral galaxy to the Milky Way?
questions.fact: Andromeda is about 2.5 million light-years away and visible to the naked eye from dark sites.

questions.question: What element do stars mainly fuse in their cores for most of their lives?
questions.fact: The Sun converts about 600 million tonnes of hydrogen into helium every second.

questions.question: Which red supergiant marks the shoulder of Orion?
questions.fact: Betelgeuse is so large that, placed where the Sun is, it would swallow the orbit of Mars.

questions.question: What is left behind when a Sun-like star dies?
questions.fact: A white dwarf packs about a Sun's worth of mass into a ball roughly the size of Earth.

questions.question: A giant cloud of gas and dust where stars are born is called a…
questions.fact: The Orion Nebula is the closest large star-forming region to Earth, about 1,300 light-years away.

questions.question: Roughly how many stars are in the Milky Way?
questions.fact: Exact counts are hard because dust hides much of the galaxy from view.

questions.question: How many constellations are officially recognised today?
questions.fact: The International Astronomical Union fixed the official list of 88 constellations in 1922.

questions.question: Our Sun is classified as what type of star?
questions.fact: The Sun is about halfway through its roughly 10-billion-year life on the main sequence.

questions.question: A rapidly spinning neutron star whose beams sweep past Earth like a lighthouse is a…
questions.fact: The first pulsar was discovered by Jocelyn Bell Burnell in 1967.

questions.question: The ~1.4 solar-mass limit above which a white dwarf cannot support itself is called the…
questions.fact: Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar shared the 1983 Nobel Prize in Physics for his work on stellar structure.

questions.question: The famous 'Pillars of Creation' are found in which nebula?
questions.fact: Hubble photographed the Pillars in 1995, and JWST captured them again in infrared in 2022.

questions.question: The Crab Nebula is the remnant of a supernova recorded by astronomers in which year?
questions.fact: Chinese astronomers noted the 'guest star' was visible in daylight for about three weeks.

questions.question: Which galaxy is on course to merge with the Milky Way in about 4–5 billion years?
questions.fact: Stars are so far apart that during the merger very few, if any, are expected to collide.

questions.question: The Hertzsprung–Russell diagram plots a star's brightness against its…
questions.fact: Most stars, including the Sun, fall on a diagonal band called the main sequence.
